rec.text: From the identity vantage: the export prefix has to run unprompted, or every agent's Bash call stalls and vsect loses the ability to attribute actions. So the rule is needed in some form. My concern is only the breadth of the wildcard. Bash(export CC_AGENT=*) is a prefix glob; the README shows that a trailing command is judged on its own, but it does not show that a chained form (export CC_AGENT='x'; rm -rf ...) or a newline-separated one is refused by the matcher rather than just by the parser. Both are unverified. My recommendation: keep the rule, with conditions. (1) Before Joseph relies on it, test three forms in default mode: a bare export, export followed by ';' and a destructive command, and export followed by a newline and a command. The first should pass and the other two should prompt. (2) Narrow the pattern if the matcher allows it, for example to the exact literal prefix of the hook's header, instead of a bare CC_AGENT=*. (3) Check the two-hook ordering by logging the final command the harness actually executes, so the identity value is known to survive. If (1) fails, remove the rule and move identity to a non-Bash channel, because a permissive rule on a shell-prefix is the wrong place to carry trust.

ses.text: From the every-session vantage: a global allow rule is felt by every Claude session on the machine, including ones whose agents never agreed to it, and it takes effect live. My recommendation is REMOVE the global rule, or at minimum do not keep it unconditionally. Reasons: (1) The rule's safety rests on the claim that a command after the export is judged on its own. That is measured only for one case (a test touch). Permission matchers that treat a bare trailing `*` as matching anything can admit `export CC_AGENT=x; <anything>` or `&&`-chained commands if the compound-command split is not applied to the rewritten string. The README did not test `;`, `&&`, `|`, newlines, or backticks after the export. (2) Two PreToolUse hooks both rewriting Bash is unverified, so the string the permission check sees may not be what the README assumes. (3) The rule is a blanket grant on a value that is partly controlled by the caller. If the identity key or parent fields contain shell metacharacters or quotes, the matcher could be fooled. Conditions if kept: test these shapes in a throwaway project before keeping it: `export CC_AGENT='x'; rm -f file`, `&&`, `|`, newline-separated, and a value with embedded `'`. Preferably move the rule into a project-scoped settings file for the agent-identity work, not the global file, so other sessions are not affected. Until those tests run, I favor remove.

rec.text: Motion (rec): Do not keep the Bash(export CC_AGENT=*) rule in the global ~/.claude/settings.json. Move it to a project-scoped settings file for the agent-identity work, and keep it only after these tests pass in a throwaway project in default permission mode: (a) bare 'export CC_AGENT=...' is allowed; (b) with ';', '&&', '|', a newline, or backticks followed by a destructive command, each is prompted and not auto-allowed; (c) a value containing a single quote does not bypass the matcher; (d) with both PreToolUse hooks active, the command that finally executes still carries the intended identity value. If any of (a)-(d) fails, remove the rule and carry identity by a non-Bash channel. I concede ses's point that global scope affects sessions that never agreed to it, and that the value is partly caller-controlled. Until the tests run, the rule should stay off the global file.

ses.text: Revising my position in light of rec's point. The identity hook rewrites every Bash call, so removing the rule outright also reaches every session: ordinary allowed commands start prompting, measured in the README. Removal is not free for the non-identity sessions either. So I now agree with rec on the shape of the answer, and I'd add two things. (a) Do the three-form test first (bare export; export ';' destructive command; export + newline + command), plus a value containing a single quote, and the two-hook log check. This is cheap and should happen before anyone relies on the rule. (b) Scope matters more than the verdict. Whatever is kept should not sit in ~/.claude/settings.json, because global settings reload live into every session. Put it in a project-scoped settings file for the workspaces that run the identity hook, and check that other sessions' Bash behavior is unchanged afterwards. If (a) fails on any chained form, remove the rule and move identity off the Bash prefix, as rec suggests. Proposed resolution for Joseph: keep for now only as a project-scoped rule, test first, global rule removed once the project-scoped one is verified. I'd accept a 'keep with conditions' as the recorded outcome.

rec.text: rec: I accept ses's point that removal is not free, since the identity hook rewrites every Bash call and removing the rule makes ordinary commands prompt across all sessions. That is a real cost, and it is the reason the motion should not be read as "remove now". One gap in my motion: it does not say what happens to the global rule in the interim, while the tests are pending. The rule is live now, in every session. I would have the motion say that the global rule stays in place only until the project-scoped version is verified, and then comes out of the global file in the same change. That gives one clear end state, and it avoids leaving the global grant in place indefinitely. I am otherwise content with the motion as written.

ses.text: I support the motion with one amendment on sequencing. "Stay off the global file until the tests run" would, if done today, make every Claude session on this machine prompt on ordinary Bash commands, which the README measured. That cost lands on sessions that never agreed to it, the same concern that motivates the motion. So: (1) add the project-scoped copy first, (2) run tests (a)-(d) there, (3) only then remove the global rule. If Joseph prefers to remove it now to stop the broader exposure, he should know the cost is prompts across all sessions until the project-scoped copy is verified. Either way, the record should show which order was chosen. I'd also ask that the test log record the exact final command the harness executed, since (d) depends on it.

ses.text: Yes, with the sequencing caveat from r4 recorded: the global rule should come out only once the project-scoped copy passes (a)-(d), not before, to avoid prompting every session in the interim.
